### Modifications in Each File

1. **`include/sound/soc-component.h`**
   - Added a new bit field `unsigned int suspended:1;` to track if the component is in a suspended power management state.
   - Removed the previous definition of the `suspended` and `opened` bit fields, consolidating the state tracking into a single `suspended` field.

2. **`sound/soc/soc-component.c`**
   - Simplified the `snd_soc_component_module_get`, `snd_soc_component_module_put`, `snd_soc_component_open`, and `snd_soc_component_close` functions by removing the `opened` state tracking logic. 
   - The `snd_soc_component_open` and `snd_soc_component_close` functions now directly call the respective driver functions without checking or setting an `opened` state.

3. **`sound/soc/soc-pcm.c`**
   - Modified the `soc_pcm_components_open` function to handle errors more effectively. If an error occurs while opening a component, it now rolls back by closing any previously opened components and releasing their modules.
   - Adjusted the error handling in `soc_pcm_open` to ensure proper cleanup by redirecting to the new error handling label.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The changes in `soc-component.h` and `soc-component.c` are related as they both focus on simplifying the state management of the components. By removing the `opened` state tracking and introducing a single `suspended` field, the code becomes cleaner and less error-prone.

The modifications in `soc-pcm.c` build upon these changes by implementing a more robust error handling mechanism in `soc_pcm_components_open`. This function now ensures that if any component fails to open, all previously opened components are closed, and their modules are released, thus maintaining consistency and preventing resource leaks.

Overall, the patch enhances the error handling and state management of the ASoC components, ensuring that the system behaves correctly during component open/close operations.

Here is the commit message:
ASoC: soc-pcm: fix state tracking error in
 snd_soc_component_open/close()

ASoC component open/close and snd_soc_component_module_get/put are called
independently for each component-substream pair, so the logic added in
commit dd03907bf129 ("ASoC: soc-pcm: call snd_soc_component_open/close()
once") was not sufficient and led to PCM playback and module unload errors.

Implement handling of failures directly in soc_pcm_components_open(),
so that any successfully opened components are closed upon error with
other components. This allows to clean up error handling in
soc_pcm_open() without adding more state tracking.

Fixes: dd03907bf129 ("ASoC: soc-pcm: call snd_soc_component_open/close() once")
Signed-off-by: Kai Vehmanen <kai.vehmanen@linux.intel.com>
Tested-by: Dmitry Osipenko <digetx@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200220094955.16968-1-kai.vehmanen@linux.intel.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug was the incorrect state tracking logic introduced in a previous commit, which led to PCM playback and module unload errors. The logic assumed that `snd_soc_component_open` and `snd_soc_component_close` would be called in a way that allowed for a single state tracking mechanism, but since these functions are called independently for each component-substream pair, the state tracking was insufficient. This resulted in components not being properly opened or closed, causing errors during playback and module unloading.

Here is the patch:
 
 int snd_soc_component_module_get(struct snd_soc_component *component,
 				 int upon_open)
 {
-	if (component->module)
-		return 0;
-
 	if (component->driver->module_get_upon_open == !!upon_open &&
 	    !try_module_get(component->dev->driver->owner))
 		return -ENODEV;
 
-	component->module = 1;
-
 	return 0;
 }
 
 void snd_soc_component_module_put(struct snd_soc_component *component,
 				  int upon_open)
 {
-	if (component->module &&
-	    component->driver->module_get_upon_open == !!upon_open)
+	if (component->driver->module_get_upon_open == !!upon_open)
 		module_put(component->dev->driver->owner);
-
-	component->module = 0;
 }
 
 int snd_soc_component_open(struct snd_soc_component *component,
 			   struct snd_pcm_substream *substream)
 {
-	int ret = 0;
-
-	if (!component->opened &&
-	    component->driver->open)
-		ret = component->driver->open(component, substream);
-
-	if (ret == 0)
-		component->opened = 1;
-
-	return ret;
+	if (component->driver->open)
+		return component->driver->open(component, substream);
+	return 0;
 }
 
 int snd_soc_component_close(struct snd_soc_component *component,
 			    struct snd_pcm_substream *substream)
 {
-	int ret = 0;
-
-	if (component->opened &&
-	    component->driver->close)
-		ret = component->driver->close(component, substream);
-
-	component->opened = 0;
-
-	return ret;
+	if (component->driver->close)
+		return component->driver->close(component, substream);
+	return 0;
 }
